description: Known failures of the Azure Local ARM Validate and Deploy, matched against the failing step of the deployment steps tree. Read by scripts/common/arm-deployment/AzlArmDeploymentRun.psm1. Add an entry when a failure is understood; the run then prints the cause and the remediation and writes the id into the event feed (DeploymentFailed.knownIssue). Nothing here is executed.

fields.id: Stable identifier; goes into events and reports.
fields.title: One line.
fields.phase: Validate, Deploy, or both. The entry only matches a failure in these phases.
fields.match: All given members must match (regular expressions, case-insensitive). stepId is the portal's step number as text (the fullStepIndex, for example 0.41), stepName the step's name, error the step's exception text and the ARM error message together. At least one member is required.
fields.affectedBuilds: Optional. OS build prefixes (12.2690.) for which the issue is known; a match is still reported for other builds, but marked as not yet seen on that build.
fields.retry: What the tool may do next. none: do not resubmit until the cause is fixed. after-fix: resubmit (Deploy: resume) after the remediation. resubmit-once: safe to submit the same thing once more without a fix (a transient error). no-validate: never run Validate again for this instance (Deploy resume only).
fields.confidence: documented (Microsoft Learn says so), observed (seen on our own deployments, evidence given), pattern (matched by name or error text, not seen in a run yet).

issues.title: Deploy fails at the Arc infrastructure step because the Arc machine is named after the device ID
issues.cause: Simplified machine provisioning names each Arc machine <device-id>-1, not the host name. On build 2690 the step that deploys the Arc infrastructure components looks the Arc machine up by the host name (the computer name) and does not find it (ParentResourceNotFound). Validate does not reach this step, so Validate passes. A Microsoft bug; no documented workaround.
remediation: Do not run Validate again for this instance (license sync).
Check the precondition ArcMachineNaming before Deploy: it reports every node whose Arc machine name is not its host name.
Route A: wait for a Microsoft build that fixes the lookup, then Resume the Deploy.
Route B: install the nodes from the Microsoft image and register them with Azure Arc under the host name (the OS configuration run does this for ISO-installed nodes), then Validate and Deploy.
Send the failed step, the Arc machine names and the build to Microsoft support.
issues.evidence: tierpointpoc 2026-10 (nic26-clus01) and 2026-11-06: Validate passed after ZTP, Deploy failed at step 0.41 (Deploy Arc infrastructure components, ParentResourceNotFound) on 12.2690.1003.15. tierpointpoc/.ai/memory/DECISIONS.md, docs/discovery-report.md.

issues.title: Deploy fails at step 0.41 (any text): device-ID Arc machine names are the first thing to rule out
issues.cause: Step 0.41 is where the 2026-11-06 deployment on build 2690 stopped. If the Arc machines are named <device-id>-1, it is the same Microsoft bug as arc-device-id-name even when the error text is different or empty.
remediation: Look at the Arc machine names in the resource group. If they are not the host names, follow arc-device-id-name.
If they are the host names, copy the step's error text from the portal (Deployments, error details) to Microsoft support and add the text to this file.

issues.title: The portal or the validation reports an unsupported OS version

match.error: Unsupported OS version|OS version .*(not supported|unsupported)|not a supported (OS|operating system) version

issues.cause: The OS build on the machines is not one the service accepts for a new deployment in this subscription and release train (an older build, a build that is not in the catalog the subscription is entitled to, or machines on different builds). Seen on our lab: build 2609 is refused for new deployments, 2690 is a prerelease that only the entitled subscription accepts.
remediation: Read the build on every node (the OS configuration report and the Arc machine's osVersion) and compare with the build the design pins (hardware or solution version in infrastructure.yml, the ZTP handoff's vsrVersion).
Install the build the deployment accepts on every node. All nodes must run the same build; mixed builds fail the machine validation.
For a prerelease build, deploy only in the subscription that is entitled to it.
Run Validate again only if the instance is not in a failed deployment state.
issues.evidence: tierpointpoc DECISIONS.md decision 2 (Validate refuses 2609 for new deployments). The exact portal text is not on Microsoft Learn.

issues.title: Registration or provisioning error 5901 (403 on the target Arc machine)
issues.cause: The service identity got HTTP 403 on the target Arc machine, although the role assignment existed. Seen for about 21 minutes after the role was assigned; the same request passed after a resubmit. Cause unconfirmed (role assignment propagation is the suspect).
remediation: Check the role assignments at the resource group (Azure Connected Machine Resource Manager and the Azure Local roles) and that the assignment is a few minutes old, not seconds.
Wait 5 to 10 minutes and submit again once. For a Deploy, resume instead of starting over.
If it fails again, collect the correlation ID of the error and open a support ticket.
issues.evidence: tierpointpoc docs/design.md, 'The 5901 on node 1': resubmit passed it.

issues.title: Role assignment already exists
issues.cause: The deployment was tried from the portal first in the same resource group, so another identity already holds the equivalent role assignment and the template cannot create it.
remediation: The failed resource names the role assignment (for example AzureStackHCIDeviceManagementRole-RoleAssignment).
In the resource group, open Access control (IAM), Role assignments, find the assignment of that role and delete it.
Submit the deployment again.
issues.evidence: Microsoft Learn, ARM template deployment, known issues.

issues.title: Tenant ID, application ID, principal ID, and scope aren't allowed to be updated

match.error: aren.t allowed to be updated|not allowed to be updated|RoleAssignmentUpdateNotPermitted

issues.cause: Zombie role assignments: a former deployment's resources were deleted, but its role assignments stayed in the resource group.
remediation: Access control (IAM), Role assignments, filter Type: Unknown. Assignments shown as 'Identity not found' are the zombies.
Delete them and submit again.
issues.evidence: Microsoft Learn, ARM template deployment, known issues.

issues.title: Another Validate after a failed deployment resets the system properties (license sync)
issues.cause: Starting a deployment in Validate mode while the instance is in the Deployment failed state resets its system properties, which can break license sync.
remediation: Do not run Validate again. Fix the cause of the failed deployment and resume the Deploy.
If a Validate already ran, open a support ticket before doing anything else.
issues.evidence: Microsoft Learn, ARM template deployment, known issues.

issues.title: Active Directory preparation is missing or incomplete (OU, LCM user, GPO, permissions)

match.error: ExternalActiveDirectory|AD OU|Active Directory (preparation|prerequisite|validat)|organizational unit|OU path|LCM (user|admin).*(not found|denied|invalid)|Cannot find an object with identity

issues.cause: The Active Directory preparation tool was not run, or the OU path or the LCM user in the deployment does not match what it created, or the deployment user lacks rights on the OU.
remediation: Run the precondition ActiveDirectoryPrepared (it checks the OU and the LCM user named in infrastructure.yml from a domain-joined host), or Invoke-AzStackHciExternalActiveDirectoryValidation from a domain-joined machine.
Check identity.active_directory.ou_path (not the top level of the domain) and identity.active_directory.lcm_user.username (20 characters at most) against what the preparation tool created.
Check that the LCM user can create computer objects in the OU (GenericAll on the OU) and that no GPO blocks it.
Submit again after the fix.
issues.evidence: Learn: Environment Checker, Active Directory validator. The text patterns have not been seen in one of our runs yet.

issues.title: A node or the deployment cannot resolve a name (domain controller, Azure endpoint, NTP)

match.error: No such host is known|name resolution|could not be resolved|DNS (server|resolution|lookup)|Unable to find a default server with Active Directory Web Services

issues.cause: The DNS servers in networking.management.dns_servers do not resolve the domain (Active Directory) or the Azure endpoints, or a node still holds a DHCP DNS setting. For Active Directory the domain controller's Active Directory Web Services (TCP 9389) may also be unreachable.
remediation: Run the OS configuration verification again (DNS and Time steps) and read the DNS servers each node reports.
From a node: Resolve-DnsName <domain_fqdn> -Server <dns server>; Test-NetConnection <domain controller> -Port 9389.
Fix networking.management.dns_servers or the DNS records, apply the OS configuration, submit again.
issues.evidence: Learn Q&A on ADWS; environment validator descriptions. The patterns have not been seen in one of our runs yet.

issues.title: The selected physical network adapter is not bound to the management virtual switch

match.error: not binded to the management virtual switch|not bound to the management virtual switch

issues.cause: A failed validation left cloud-side switch data (the validation's temporary VM switch) in the Edge device resource, and the Device Management extension did not notice that the switch was deleted.
remediation: Follow Microsoft's steps: remove the validation VM switch, restart DeviceManagementService on the node, check the edgeDevices resource, then submit again.
Do not keep retrying Validate; every retry makes the stale data worse.
issues.evidence: Microsoft Learn, Troubleshoot Azure portal deployment validation issues.

issues.title: Arc registration fails with AZCM0044: the Arc resource already exists
issues.cause: A machine was registered under this name before (an earlier try, a rebuilt node) and its Arc resource is still in the resource group, so Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization stops with AZCM0044.
remediation: The OS configuration run deletes the stale Arc resource when it is NOT Connected and registers again (up to three tries). A Connected Arc machine is never deleted: it is the registration, and the run goes on.
If you register by hand: delete the stale machine resource of the node in the Azure portal or with az connectedmachine delete, then run the registration again.
Do not delete an Arc machine that is Connected unless you mean to re-register that node.
issues.evidence: azl-toolkit lessons (proven repo): tplabs re-registration after a node rebuild.

issues.title: Arc registration is refused: AZCM0042 or HTTP 401
issues.cause: The Azure token handed to the node was refused or had expired (a long registration, a token minted for another tenant or cloud, or an account without Azure Connected Machine Onboarding on the resource group).
remediation: The OS configuration run takes a new token from its sign-in and registers again (up to three tries).
If it is refused again: sign in to the right tenant and cloud (Connect-AzAccount) with an account that has Azure Connected Machine Onboarding and Reader on the resource group, then run again.
issues.evidence: azl-toolkit lessons (proven repo): token expiry during a long bootstrap.

issues.title: Arc registration fails with 0x8009030e: the logon session does not exist
issues.cause: The credential did not carry into the remote session (a second hop, CredSSP or a delegated credential, or a session kept open across a restart).
remediation: The OS configuration run opens a new WinRM session with the local administrator (Negotiate) and registers again.
Use the local administrator of the node, not a delegated or CredSSP credential, and do not reuse a session across a restart.

issues.title: Arc registration ends with "I/O operation has been aborted" while the node restarts
issues.cause: The node restarts in the middle of the Arc bootstrap (the agent install asks for it), so the remote call is cut. The registration itself usually carries on or finishes after the restart.
remediation: The OS configuration run does NOT register again: it waits for the node to answer and for its Arc machine to be Connected.
Registering again while the node restarts is what creates the stale resource of AZCM0044. Wait, then read the Arc machine status.
issues.evidence: azl-toolkit lessons (proven repo): a node reboot during the bootstrap.

issues.title: Validate fails at step 0.60 (InvokeEnvironmentChecker): the SBE is not validated with the solution version

match.error: ErrorUnvalidatedSolutionAndSbeCombination|has not been validated with Solution version

issues.cause: Azure checks the SBE package and its manifest against the solution version the deployment installs, and refuses an SBE that the OEM has not validated with that solution (ErrorUnvalidatedSolutionAndSbeCombination). The message names the SBE, the solution version and the SBE packages that are validated. The failure shows after about 13 minutes of Validate. The OEM's SBE discovery catalog (Dell: SBE_Discovery_Dell.xml, https://aka.ms/AzureStackSBEUpdate/DellEMC) lists, per SBE version and family, the solution versions it is validated with (RequiredPackages, Type Solution, wildcards such as 12.*.1004.*). The precondition SbeConsistent only checks that an SBE is set, so it does not catch this; SbeValidatedWithSolution does.
remediation: Read the precondition SbeValidatedWithSolution in the plan report: it compares hardware.sbe.version and hardware.sbe.family with the solution version (run setting solutionVersion, the ZTP handoff, or the nodes' OS build) using the SBE discovery catalog, and names the SBE versions of the family that are validated.

Download the validated SBE from the OEM's support site (Dell support for AX nodes), put it in hardware.sbe.bundle_path with its .xml and SBE_Discovery_*.xml, and set hardware.sbe.version (and hardware.sbe.family if it differs).
Run the OS configuration (Invoke-AzureLocalOsConfiguration.ps1 -Mode Apply) so the package is delivered to C:\SBE on every node.
Alternatively pin the solution version (provisioning.os_version) that the SBE you have is validated for, and install that build on the nodes.
Run Validate again; the instance is not in a failed deployment state after this error.
issues.evidence: tplabs lab 2026-11-08, validate-3 (arm-report/validate-3/summary.md): step 0.60 InvokeEnvironmentChecker, SBE_Dell_16G-45n0c-Intel_5.0.2606.1616 with Solution version 12.2610.1004.50; Azure listed SBE_Dell_17G-Intel_5.0.2609.1715, SBE_Dell_16G-45n0c-Intel_5.0.2609.1611, SBE_Dell_AX-15G_5.0.2609.1511 and SBE_Dell_AX-14G_5.0.2609.1409 as validated. Dell's catalog (SBE_Discovery_Dell.xml, 2026-10-21) gives 5.0.2606.1616 Solution 12.*.1003.* and 12.*.1002.*, 5.0.2609.1611 Solution 12.*.1004.* and 12.*.1003.*.
